response.sql:
WITH high_fees AS (
  SELECT f.feesnode, f.feerate, f.rebrate, f.orderslink, o.dealedge
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    dealedge,
    AVG(feerate - rebrate) as group_avg_net_fee,
    COUNT(*) as record_count
  FROM high_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
),
side_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    dealedge,
    AVG(group_avg_net_fee) as side_average
  FROM group_stats
  GROUP BY dealedge
)
SELECT 
  gs.orderslink,
  gs.dealedge,
  gs.group_avg_net_fee,
  gs.record_count,
  gs.group_avg_net_fee - sa.side_average as difference
FROM group_stats gs
JOIN side_averages sa ON gs.dealedge = sa.dealedge
WHERE gs.group_avg_net_fee > sa.side_average
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: "high-rate fee records, with 0.0009 on the fee rate as the cutoff" is interpreted as feerate >= 0.0009. Could be feerate > 0.0009 if cutoff means the strict boundary above which records qualify.

alternatives.interpretation: If cutoff 0.0009 means the strict lower boundary (feerate > 0.0009 rather than >=)
